messages:
Maya: Quick heads-up — DeployBot reported a mixed tenant-pin state during the v2 rollout to prod. Need an operator decision on tie-break behavior (prefer header vs. fallback route). :eyes:

deploy-bot: Canary started for route `api.v2` (canary=5% traffic). Pin snapshot: 23 tenants pinned to v1, 4 tenants pinned to v2, 12 unpinned. See /deploybot/logs/1765.

Tyler: What does "mixed pin state" mean for routing? Are requests from pinned tenants still going to v1?

Maya: Right now routing honors tenant pin header when present, but we have a fallback policy that can also use the route feature-flag if header missing. The deployflow found headers set inconsistently (some proxies stripping header).

Priya: Which tenants are affected? Any enterprise customers in that list? We should avoid surprise breaks during the change window.

Zach: Quick telemetry: pinned-v1 tenants account for ~0.4% of global qps but include 2 large enterprise accounts (alpha-tenant-3, beta-corp). Error budget for those is tight.

Sara: Release note implication: v2 changes include header-case normalization for `X-API-Version` and a small response schema tweak (streamed metadata field renamed). If proxies are dropping headers, those tenants could get v2 responses unexpectedly. Need doc + support note.

Maya: Proposal A: Keep current behavior (honor header if present, else route by new policy). Proposal B: Strict pin tiebreak — if any pin exists for tenant, always route to pinned version (override fallback). Proposal C: Force canary pause until ops can confirm proxy headers across CDNs.

Tyler: I'd lean B for safety (prefer pinned version). It prevents accidental migration due to header stripping. Downside: slows rollout for unpinned users behind same tenant id.

ops_lead: Operational constraints — switching to strict pin (B) requires a quick deploybot config flip. We can do it now, but must notify release-signal and support, and freeze any auto-scaling changes for 45m.

Priya: If we pick B, we should also do a short targeted test: 1) pin replicate for alpha-tenant-3 to v1 for 10m, 2) confirm error/latency stable, 3) unpin and re-run canary. Can ops script that?

Zach: Metrics guardrails proposal: rollback if 3m error rate delta > 0.8% for pinned tenants OR 1% global 5xx increase, or latency p95 increase > 200ms.

Maya: Agreed. Ownering: Maya for pin decision, Tyler for telemetry checks, Priya for release notes & support blurb, ops_lead to flip deploybot policy and run pin/unpin. Sara to update docs about header normalization.

deploy-bot: Command summary available: `./deploybot config set pin_tiebreak strict && ./deploybot pin tenant=alpha-tenant-3 target=v1 reason="compat-check" --expires 10m`

ops_lead: I'm running the commands now.

ops_lead: `deploybot config set pin_tiebreak strict` -> success. Can verify with `deploybot config get pin_tiebreak` — returns `strict`.

ops_lead: Pinning alpha-tenant-3 to v1 for 10m... -> success.

Tyler: Running telemetry check script: `./tools/telemetry/compare --route api.v2 --tenants alpha-tenant-3,beta-corp --window 10m`

Zach: Early signal: no error spike in first 5m for alpha-tenant-3. Latency p95 +12ms. beta-corp data later (10m window) showing stable.

Priya: Drafting support note now: short blurb about header normalization and tenant pins. Adding a line in release notes: "Customers pinned to v1 will continue to be routed to v1; we will not auto-upgrade pinned tenants during this rollout."

Maya: OK — since checks are green and ops flipped to strict, proceed with canary at 5% with strict pin tiebreak. Hold for 30m observation before increasing traffic. If any guardrail trips we rollback to previous config and pause rollout.

Sara: I'll update the docs and post the support message to #support and #customers-notice.

deploy-bot: Canary running (5%). Watching metrics: next automated checkpoint in 15m.

Priya: Support note posted to #support (msg id 5432). Linking to internal KB: /docs/v2-header-change.

Maya: Thanks. If anything odd appears ping @ops_lead and @Maya immediately. :thumbsup:

deploy-bot: Automated checkpoint at +15m: no guardrail breaches detected. Continuing.

Maya: After 30m observation we can reconvene and either expand to 25% or hold. Logging decision here: strict pin tiebreak engaged, release notes updated, support notified.

Tyler: Marking telemetry checks as passed for this window. I'll follow up with a 1h post-mortem if any anomalies.

ops_lead: Leaving the strict setting in place until full rollout completes. If release owners want it reverted for faster rollout we need a formal approval call.

Maya: Closing thread for now — will reopen if we see issues. Thanks all. :white_check_mark:
